title: Remember God Before Life Fades
overview: The Teacher urges young people to remember God before old age and death arrive, and the book then closes with a word about the Teacher and a short summary of what matters.

parts.label: Remember while young (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: The call is to keep God in mind early, before the hard years come when life gives little pleasure. Lights going dark and clouds returning after rain picture a time when one trouble follows another with little relief.

parts.label: A portrait of growing old (vv. 3-5)
parts.note: Most readers take these images as the aging body: trembling hands, bent legs, few teeth left to grind food, dim eyes, light sleep, faint hearing and white hair like almond blossoms. Some details, like the dragging grasshopper, are uncertain, and the scene ends with a funeral, where mourners were often hired to walk the streets.

parts.label: The moment of death (vv. 6-7)
parts.note: A precious lamp crashes when its cord snaps, and a jar and wheel at a well break so no more water can be drawn, both pictures of life ending. The body returns to dust and the breath of life goes back to God who gave it, though how much this says about life after death is debated.

parts.label: The opening cry returns (v. 8)
parts.note: The main section ends with the same words the book began with. The Hebrew word, often translated "meaningless" or "vanity," literally means breath or vapor, and many scholars think it stresses how fleeting and hard to grasp life is, though its exact sense here is debated.

parts.label: About the Teacher (vv. 9-12)
parts.note: Here someone speaks about the Teacher, likely an editor in the view of many scholars, praising him as a careful collector and writer of true sayings. Wise words are like goads, the sharp sticks used to prod oxen, and like nails driven firm, given by one shepherd, which most take to mean God.

parts.label: The final summary (vv. 13-14)
parts.note: The conclusion is to revere God and keep his commands, because God will judge every act, even hidden ones, good or bad. It offers a fixed point after a book full of hard questions.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether the closing verses sum up what the Teacher meant all along or are a later voice gently correcting his bleaker conclusions.
think: If you pictured your own later years honestly, what would you want to have given your attention to while you still had the strength?
